strategy.title: Cold-email fixed-scope website rebuilds to local service businesses at $1,500, builds subcontracted to a Freelancer.com developer at $377
strategy.why: Highest contribution per deal of the discovered routes ($1,500 - $377 build - ~$88 Stripe fees = ~$1,035), so 12 deals clear $12,000 after all direct costs inside 45 days with peak owner exposure ~$1,662 < $2,500 (deposits fund later batches). Comparable builds are posted at $750-1500 and bid at $366-835, so both the price ceiling and the subcontract supply are visible; the unknown is whether cold-reached local businesses pay $1,500, which only a live test measures.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL on cold-emailed $1,500 rebuilds is a startable shape and the money arithmetic fits the limits, but the schedule the test is supposed to validate is not carried by its own threshold, the price is presented as more supported than it is, and the members list contradicts the strategy.
findings: Recomputed economics: Stripe 2.9% + $0.30 on each $750 half = $22.05, $44.10 per deal (the ledger's $88.20 per batch of four deposits matches that); contribution per deal = 1,500 - 377 - 44 = $1,079; 12 deals = $12,947, less $154 tools = $12,793 >= $12,000. Exposure: $154 + 4 x $377 floated on day 9 while deposits sit in Stripe's first payout until day 22 = $1,662 (Brain trace peak $1,927) <= $2,500. These fit.

Reach vs schedule: Instantly Growth uploads 1,000 contacts per month (src_instantly), so by day 26 - when the ledger has all 12 deposits in - at most ~1,000 contacts have been reached. 12 deposits from 1,000 contacts is a 1.2% paid rate, while the threshold (2 of 300 = 0.67%) only implies ~6.7 deals by day 26 and ~13 only after all 2,000 contacts, i.e. after day 31, leaving month-2 deals to deposit, deliver in 7 days and settle balances by day 45. Rebuild the ledger on the threshold rate, or raise the threshold to what the 12-by-day-26 schedule needs (about 4 of 300), and show that batch 3 settles by day 45 either way.

Proof and stop disagree: proof says '>= 2 paid deposits from <= 1,000 businesses reached by day 10', stop says 'fewer than 2 from the first 300 by day 10'. Pick one denominator; at 1,000 contacts per month only ~300 are reachable by day 10.

Price: the strategy says 'comparable builds are posted at $750-1500 and bid at $366-835, so the price ceiling ... is visible'. Those are open budgets and sellers' bids on Freelancer.com, rejected on verification as buyer-paid prices, from marketplace posters, not cold-reached US local businesses; $1,500 sits at the top of one poster's budget. q_price is correctly ASSUMED - the strategy text should say the same.

Members list includes cop_a11a (described as a duplicate kept out), cop_8e4f and cop_e36c (described as alternatives) with deal counts; only cop_02da is the plan. Remove them or the ledger double-counts buyers.

Order: s4 (offers) does not depend on s1 (the developer quote due day 4). Deposits start day 8, so no order is taken before the quote deadline in practice, but make s4 depend on s1 so the stop 'no quote <= $377 by day 4: do not sell' is enforced.
s1, s3, s4 rely on SEND_A_MESSAGE (NOT_CONNECTED) and READ_REPLIES (UNREAD): name the owner as sender with hours, or state how Brain sends. No owner-hours cap, but unknown hours are unknown.

conditions.why: No EVIDENCE fact holds a price buyers paid; the Freelancer.com budgets/bids and the Clutch ceiling were rejected on verification (open budgets and sellers' asks, mismatched population).
No developer has quoted the spec; $377 is an average of other sellers' bids on another poster's project, and the offer step does not depend on the quote test.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is right and the plan is now startable and internally consistent where it matters. Price ($1,500) is explicitly ASSUMED and measured by paid deposits; the build cost is an estimate gated by a written developer quote <= $377 on day 4 before any offer (s4 depends on s1), so no order is taken before fulfilment is shown possible. Reach was fixed (Hypergrowth, 300 contacts every 3 days, 1,800 by day 20); at the threshold rate 2/300 that is 12 deposits, so passing at the threshold carries the target. The owner is the sender with stated hours (27 h; no hours cap). Members hold only the strategy opening.
findings: Recomputed: receipts 12 x $1,500 = $18,000; Stripe 24 x $22.05 = $529; builds 12 x $377 = $4,524; tools $154; contribution $12,793 >= $12,000 (headroom $793, i.e. one deal short misses the target - 11 deals = $11,714). Peak float $154 + 4 x $377 = $1,662 until batch-1 deposits settle day 23 (Brain trace peak $1,927) <= $2,500. Last balances settle day 34 < 45.

Stale text: validation.proof still reads 'By day 10 ... from <= 1,000 local businesses reached', while the stop/continue rules and threshold use the first 300 contacts judged on day 12. The rules are consistent; the proof sentence should be updated to match.
Margin is thin: the target needs all 12 deals at $377 or less; the day-18 stop (< 8 deposits from 1,200 contacts) is the right guard and should be read as 'target missed', not 'later'.

strategy.title: Cold-email fixed-scope website rebuilds to local service businesses at $1,500, builds subcontracted to a Freelancer.com developer at $377
strategy.why: Highest contribution per deal of the discovered routes ($1,500 - $377 build - ~$88 Stripe fees = ~$1,035), so 12 deals clear $12,000 after all direct costs inside 45 days with peak owner exposure ~$1,662 < $2,500 (deposits fund later batches). The $1,500 price is ASSUMED: no record shows a cold-reached local business paying it (Freelancer.com budgets and seller bids were rejected as buyer-paid prices, and are a different population). The $377 build cost is an estimate from other seller bids, not a quote. The plan therefore tests the quote first (day 4), then the paid-deposit rate (day 12), before any order is placed.
